as_printed: Joachim Breitner, "Reservoir sampling with few random bits" (blog post)
canonical: Joachim Breitner, "Reservoir sampling with few random bits," personal blog post, published 2018-03-25, https://www.joachim-breitner.de/blog/737-Reservoir_sampling_with_few_random_bits (with a 2-comment reader thread, most recently 2019-01-31)
note: Fetched the live page in full. It is a personal blog post on Joachim Breitner's homepage (Published 2018-03-25, tags 'English'/'Math'), NOT a peer-reviewed venue, and it carries a comment thread with two reader replies (Benjamin Price, 2018-04-18; Christoph Pfister, 2019-01-31). IMPORTANT: Breitner's own post body does NOT give a closed form for the bit cost -- it ends with an open question ('What is the expected number of coin throws for n prisoners? Does this number converge to log(n) ...?'). The closed form quoted in the task appears only in the second reader COMMENT, by Christoph Pfister (2019-01-31), under the comment's own '### Asymptotics' subheading. Verbatim quote from that location: "H(X2, X3, …, Xn) = H_b(1/2) + H_b(1/3) + ⋯ + H_b(1/n), where H_b denotes the binary entropy function. Consequently, it is not difficult to show that H(X2, X3, …, Xn) = log2 n + ∑ k=2…n (1/k)⋅log2(k−1). Asymptotically, this behaves like (ln n)2/(2⋅ln 2), i.e., lim n→∞ (H(X2, X3, …, Xn))/((ln n)2/(2⋅ln 2)) = 1." This matches the expected form H = log2(n) + sum (1/k) log2(k-1) ~ (ln n)^2/(2 ln 2), but it is a commenter's derivation (citing Knuth & Yao 1976 and Cover & Thomas), not a claim made by Breitner in the article body itself.

note: This is a pre-DOI-era book chapter (not in Crossref/arXiv), so it was cross-checked across multiple independent sources via WebSearch (Semantic Scholar record, and secondary citations in later papers such as the Breitner blog's own reference list, which cites it identically as 'D.
